title: Suzani Embroidery
summary: Suzani is the large embroidered cloth of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, worked in silk thread on cotton, with round flower-like medallions, curling vines, leaves and fruit laid out in balanced panels in crimson, indigo, gold and green.
howToPlay: Choose a thread colour and a motif from the strip under the cloth.
Touch a square to stitch it: the same motif appears in the matching squares of all four quarters, as on a cloth worked from the centre outward.
Copy the small panel shown above the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is symmetric left to right and top to bottom, so each stitch you place is copied to its three partners.
Leaves and spirals turn to follow the symmetry, as they would if sewn by hand.
A square counts only when its motif and its thread colour both match the panel; three stars need a nearly perfect copy.
heritageNote: Suzani cloths have been embroidered in the oasis towns of Central Asia, such as Bukhara, Samarkand, Shahrisabz and Tashkent, where each town has its own favoured layout; families and craft workshops still make them today.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original panels after traditional suzani medallion and vine layouts)
